title: U.S. House · California's 24th Congressional District
area: Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo counties on the Central Coast.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 elections under Proposition 50, a mid-decade redistricting measure voters approved in a November 2025 special election.
In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, Salud Carbajal won 54.4% of the vote (113,716 votes) and Bob Smith won 35.9% (75,085 votes), advancing them both to the November general election.

summary.text: Salud Carbajal is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for California's 24th District. Born in Mexico and raised in California, he is a Marine Corps Reserve veteran who served on the Santa Barbara County Board of Supervisors for 12 years before his first election to Congress in 2016. He sits on the Armed Services, Agriculture, and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

background.text: According to his House biography, he emigrated from Mexico to the United States at age 5 and worked summers as a farmworker with his father.

Became the first in his family to graduate from a university, earning a bachelor's degree from UC Santa Barbara in 1990; earned a master's degree in organizational management from Fielding Graduate University in 1994.
Served in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve from 1984 to 1992; his House biography says he was mobilized to active duty during the 1992 Gulf War.
From 1993 to 2004 worked on the staff of Santa Barbara County Supervisor Naomi Schwartz, and also worked in the Santa Barbara County Public Health Department.
Served on the Santa Barbara County Board of Supervisors from 2004 to 2016.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2016 and first took office in 2017. Committees in the 2025-2026 Congress: Armed Services, Agriculture, and Transportation and Infrastructure, where he is Ranking Member of the Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee.

His House biography says multiple bills he sponsored were signed into law, including bills responding to the 2019 Conception boat fire and promoting 'red flag' laws, and that he helped write the 2021 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law as a member of Transportation and Infrastructure.
According to his House biography, he is married to Gina and they have two children, Natasha and Michael.

priorities.text: I am committed to working across party lines to bring quality jobs to the Central Coast by investing in infrastructure, encouraging clean energy development, and embracing new technology.
I believe everyone should have access to safe and affordable housing so that people from all backgrounds can live safe and healthy lives.
I will not stop fighting to pass gun safety measures while serving in Congress.

positions.summary: Supported the Inflation Reduction Act as a major climate investment and describes climate change as an urgent challenge requiring action.
positions.quote: I believe we cannot afford inaction on the most significant challenge of our time.

positions.summary: Supports creating a public option under the Affordable Care Act to compete with private insurers and bring down costs.
positions.quote: I am supportive of legislation to create a public option under the ACA and provide much-needed competition with private industry to bring down insurance costs.

positions.summary: Authored a federal red-flag law, enacted as part of the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, and supports universal background checks and reinstating the federal assault weapons ban.
positions.quote: Congress must also pass universal background checks, a policy supported by nearly 90 percent of the American people, including the vast majority of gun owners. We must also reinstate the Assault Weapons Ban, which Congress shamefully allowed to expire in 2004.

positions.summary: Describes himself as a longtime supporter of raising the minimum wage and pay equity legislation.
positions.quote: I have been a staunch supporter of raising the minimum wage and ensuring paycheck fairness.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture, the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation; Highways and Transit subcommittees), and the House Committee on Armed Services (Strategic Forces; Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Bob Smith
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2 top-two primary with 35.9% of the vote

summary.text: Bob Smith is the Republican nominee for California's 24th District. A retired U.S. Navy officer who rose from enlisted sailor to senior officer over 26 years, he is a senior engineering fellow at a defense contractor, according to his Ballotpedia survey. He says he is running to reduce partisan division and on home ownership, defense and technology jobs.

background.text: Enlisted in the U.S. Navy in 1998 and spent five years as an enlisted technician on the AEGIS Weapon System, according to his Ballotpedia survey.
Selected for the Navy's Seaman to Admiral program, earned a B.S. in General Engineering Technology from Old Dominion University (2006), and was commissioned as an officer in 2006.
Served as a Surface Warfare Officer, including multiple combat deployments, and earned an M.S. in Systems Engineering from the Naval Postgraduate School in Monterey (2015).

Spent the rest of his career as an Engineering Duty Officer directing development programs for new Navy weapon systems; says he received the Navy's Best Engineer of the Year award for 2023 for delivering a ballistic missile defense platform. Retired from the Navy in 2024 after more than 26 years.
Currently a senior engineering fellow for a defense contractor based in Washington, D.C., according to his survey.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, finishing second with 35.9% of the vote. KEYT reported that he describes his approach as 'common sense' and that his wife is a Democrat.

priorities.text: Names home ownership and housing affordability as a top priority, saying equity has been stripped from the middle class in California.
Supports a stronger U.S. military posture, saying the country must be technologically far enough ahead that 'war with the U.S. is not an option for anyone.'
Wants to attract space-industry, AI, and fusion-energy jobs to the district and stop the loss of tech companies to other states.

positions.summary: Says housing affordability and homeownership have been stripped from the middle class and should be a top federal priority.
